question.problem: Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $-5$ and the common difference is $-1.$
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

$$
f(n)=f(1)+(n-1)d.
$$

We are told that the first term is $f(1)=-5$ and the common difference is $d=-1.$ So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)+(n-1)d \\  & =-5+(n-1)(-1) \\  & =-5-n+1 \\  & =-4-n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n)=-4-n.$
